name: ufswprobe
description: The FILESYSTEM asserted through its WRITING vnode operations -- the third and last of ufs.mod's mutually exclusive probe gates, split out of ufsvnprobe at UFS 1.12b when itrunc and its 3 KB per-level indirect-copy table took the vnode gate over the 65,536 bytes in a bank (measured: ufs.mod ships at 44,061 now against 34,283 before the increment).  It mounts disk/ufsscratch.po itself and then changes it.  CASES 860-912, THE WRITE PATH (1.12a).  What they have to catch is a write path that does NOTHING, which is why every verification is a RAW kc_blkio read under the buffer cache, under bio_strategy and under everything vfs.mod owns: a filesystem that accepts writes and touches no block leaves a volume fsck calls perfect and passes any test that reads its own writes back through the cache.  They separate the three buffer decisions -- a partial write into a block that does not exist yet must CLEAR rather than read (867/869), one into a block that does must bread or it destroys what it is not overwriting (876), and a full-block write needs neither; the indirect block built when the file passes logical block 4, checked ZERO in every entry but the one threaded (884), which is what says a block off the free list was cleared before anything pointed at it; the inode read back as BYTES so the PDP-11 encode direction is pinned rather than round-tripped (871/872); and case 893, the sequence a lost write actually takes -- read a hole, caching a buffer whose b_blkno is -1, then write it, where a write path that does not overwrite b_blkno hands bio_strategy a buffer still marked as a hole and the bytes are discarded in silence.  Cases 901-911 build a real IFLNK inode and read it back both raw and through VOP_READLINK, because nothing on this volume is a symlink and ufs_symlink is 1.12c.  CASES 920-960, TRUNCATE AND RELEASE (1.12b).  What THEY have to catch is a reclaim that frees too few blocks -- invisible by every other means, since a volume that leaks blocks reads correctly and simply fills up (apple/fgx#68 was that defect on the ProDOS side).  So the oracle is sb_tfree, read before and after and asserted EXACTLY: the file is built to cost three blocks -- logical 0, logical 4, and the single indirect that logical 4 cannot be reached without -- and 927/930/931 require all three back and itrunc's own count to agree.  Also here: the partial truncate zeroing the tail past the new EOF so a later growth cannot read it again (946); the stated divergence that GROWING is Reno's hole and not 2.11BSD's allocation (949/951); ufs_setattr as ftruncate reaching the filesystem, refusing chmod with EPERM rather than ignoring it because there is no credential to weigh it against (954); and case 939, which is vinvalbuf's whole purpose -- truncate a file, grow it again, and read logical 0, where without the invalidation getblk answers from a cached buffer whose physical block now belongs to somebody else.  IT WRITES MORE THAN ANY OTHER GATE AND PUTS IT ALL BACK, including on failure: inodes 5, 6 and 7, each checked FREE first so a volume whose layout ever changes stops the probe rather than being overwritten, and blocks off the free list against an sb_nfree of 26 so no chain block is consumed -- a consumed chain block is NOT restorable by rewriting the superblock.  AND THE ORACLE JUDGES WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND.  `ufsfsck_check.py' fscks every staged spindle once the machine has finished with it, which is the campaign plan's phase-1 arm 1 -- "mount -t ufs survives a full read/write exercise; host fgxfs fsck clean".  It works even though this probe RESTORES the volume, because the restore is SEMANTIC rather than byte for byte: a completed run puts the free list and the counts back where it found them, so anything the exercise damaged OUTSIDE what it meant to touch still shows.  Measured on two completed runs: 305 used, 3,725 free, 1,020 free inodes, identical to a fresh mkfs.  IT IS NOT SELF-SUFFICIENT and must not be read as though it were -- a run that PANICS before doing anything leaves a clean volume too, which is exactly what apple/fgx#272 did -- so this arm is worth something only beside the `ufs: ok' above it and tryprobe.sh's exit status (apple/fgx#273).

requires.reason: the writing half of the filesystem probe is compiled into ufs.mod only at kernel.ufswprobe = 1, and it is a SEPARATE GATE from kernel.ufsprobe and kernel.ufsvnprobe because the three do not fit in one 64 KB module bank -- see cfg/system.cfg for the measurement.  It is off by default because it WRITES to a disk on the boot path.  Run it with `sh tools/tryprobe.sh ufswprobe`.
